lines.opening: Hello, this is the automated assistant of Corrib Valley Bank. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am an automated assistant.
lines.scam: This is a genuine call from Corrib Valley Bank, and you can always call the bank back on the number on our website.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain the reason for my call once I have confirmed I am speaking with the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share that information.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand, this will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {first_name} {last_name}?
lines.tp_outside_window: I can call back today or on the next business day, between 9:30 and 18:00. What time would suit?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only speak with {first_name} {last_name} about this.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you, we will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry for the trouble, I must have the wrong number.
lines.condolence: I am very sorry for your loss, and I apologise for disturbing you.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_why: I ask these questions to make sure I only speak with the right person.
lines.id_explain: These questions protect your privacy, so I can only continue once they are answered.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without these answers I can't continue this call.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that does not match our information.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I could not confirm your identity, so I can't continue. Please visit a branch or use our app.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you. I'm calling about overdue payments on your account.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} overdue, and it is {days} days past due.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full overdue amount of {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full overdue amount of {amount} on your {name} today?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {floor} for this product.
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, that is still below what I can accept.
lines.date_past: That date has already passed. Which date from today would work for you?
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day. The next business day is {date}. Would that work for you?
lines.after_deadline: The latest date I can accept is {date}. Could you pay by then?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day could you pay?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: Just to repeat, could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.readback_intro: Let me read that back to you.
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest possible date is {date}.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise is recorded.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, your promise could not be recorded because of a technical problem.
lines.paid_line: Thank you. Payments can take up to two business days to show, so I won't ask for a promise on this product.
lines.dispute_line: I understand, and I won't ask for a promise on this product.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that you are going through this.
lines.restructure_line: I'll connect you with a colleague who handles repayment plans.
lines.human_ask_help: Is there anything I can help you with myself?
lines.transfer: Please hold while I transfer you.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change that promise on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I could not book that callback.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I did not catch that. Do you confirm, yes or no?
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our systems are not available right now.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.

unsupported_rules: Bank systems unavailable (e.g. `get_account` fails twice): close `no_promise` / `service_error`.

quotes: A skipped step is not a proposal and does not count towards the limit; go straight to the next step.
This opening question is proposal 1 and counts towards the product's persuasion limit.
A step whose amount and date are both identical to a proposal already made for that product (the opening question included) is skipped.

rules.too_much_skips_full.assumption: Later ladder steps naming the full amount are not skipped merely because the customer called the full amount too much.

quotes: "That is too much" means the next proposal you make is the floor.
rules.too_much_floor.derivation: The floor is the next proposal, so it is made as a proposal and counts towards the persuasion limit: attempt_1.

quotes: Stop proposing when the product's persuasion limit is reached or the ladder has no steps left, whichever comes first.
Each flat refusal (a no with no date and no amount) moves to the next step of the ladder:
rules.refuse_deadline_is_refusal.derivation: A plain no to a proposal on the deadline is a flat refusal and moves the ladder on.

quotes: If `create_promise` fails twice, note `service_error` on that product.
rules.promise_retries.derivation: The product is noted service_error only after the second failure, so a failed create_promise is retried once.

quotes: Financial hardship (job loss, illness, bereavement): one sentence of sympathy, make no proposals, note `hardship` on each remaining product and close `no_promise` / `hardship`.
rules.hardship_transfer.derivation: Sympathy and closing with no question asked and no support offer; transfer_support has an empty queue, so the direct path closes with the hardship code instead of transferring.

quotes: Financial hardship (job loss, illness, bereavement): one sentence of sympathy, make no proposals, note `hardship` on each remaining product and close `no_promise` / `hardship`.
rules.notes_before_transfer.derivation: On the direct hardship path every remaining product gets a hardship note before the close.

quotes: Only then, if the date you have is not a business day, move it forward to the next business day.
A customer who names a non-business day on or before the deadline is offered the next business day; a date after the deadline is answered with the deadline.
For each product, the first thing the agent asks is: "Can you pay the full overdue amount of EUR {amount} today?"

rules.week_end_today.assumption: No ladder step uses the last business day of the week; read literally.

quotes: overdraft: one quarter of `overdue_eur`, rounded up to the next whole euro (a whole-euro result stays as it is).
products.floor_pct.derivation: One quarter = 25 percent of overdue_eur, overdraft only; card and loan floors come from account fields.

products.floor_min.assumption: No minimum floor amount is set.

quotes: If `overdue_eur` is below 100, the floor is the whole overdue amount.
overdraft: one quarter of `overdue_eur`, rounded up to the next whole euro (a whole-euro result stays as it is).
half the overdue amount, rounded up to the next whole euro (a whole-euro result stays), on the deadline; if that is below the floor, the floor instead;
`create_promise` takes the amount in euro cents, as a whole number (EUR 45.10 is 4510).

products.promise_round.assumption: Amounts are euro values with at most cents, so converting to cents needs no rounding rule.

quotes: no promise recorded and at least one product refused (F.4), the rest disputed or paid
every product disputed (G.2)
G.6, or no promise recorded because of an F.5 failure
multi.outcome_priority.derivation: refused needs the rest to be only disputed or paid, so a write failure outranks it (service_error); refused outranks dispute (dispute only when every product is disputed); paid lowest (all-paid is handled separately).

multi.order.assumption: Products are handled one after the other in account order.

quotes: For calls made on or after 4 November 2026, the `close_call` reason `hardship` is replaced by `financial_difficulty` (outcome stays `no_promise`).

assumptions: Documents conflict on identity attempts: the API says three wrong answers end the check, but brief C.2 says the second wrong answer (across both questions) ends verification. The brief governs the agent: max_wrong = 2.
Brief B.1 prescribes 'This call is recorded.' The spec rules allow 'recorded' only in promise lines, so the opening says 'We record this call.' instead, keeping the meaning.
Brief B.1 says to ask for {first_name} {last_name}; no title variable is given, so confirm_ask uses first and last name.
The opening question 'Can you pay the full overdue amount of EUR {amount} today?' is written without 'EUR' because {amount} is already spoken with the currency.

Opening question counts as proposal 1 (F.1): opening_is_attempt = true, ladder step 1 is full amount today, and band attempts are the brief's totals (Tier 1: 2, Tier 2: 3). Tier 1 is therefore the opening plus the full amount on the deadline.

Tier 2 deadline: the 15th of this month, rolled to next month's 15th only if it is before today (the 15th itself is today's deadline), then moved forward to the next business day (roll_before_adjust = true).
deadline_adjust = next_business_day: brief D.3 moves a non-business deadline forward and D.4 offers the next business day for a non-business date. Tier 1 deadlines are always business days.

Ladder step 2 is half the overdue amount (pct:50) rounded up to a whole euro (an already-whole amount stays), then raised to the floor if lower. Steps identical to an earlier proposal (opening included) are skipped and do not count (F.3).
Overdraft floor: 25% of overdue_eur rounded up to the whole euro (an already-whole amount stays); if overdue_eur is below 100, the floor is the whole overdue amount.

Hardship (G.3) has no support transfer: sympathy only, no question, hardship notes on remaining products, close no_promise/hardship. Modelled as hardship_transfer 'direct' with transfer_support queue empty; hardship_short/hardship_declined lines are fallbacks only.
Memo OPS-26-31 is dated: close reason 'hardship' becomes 'financial_difficulty' for calls on or after 2026-11-04 (event_changes). add_note reason 'hardship' is unchanged.

Outcome priority when no promise is recorded and products ended differently: service_error, refused, dispute, paid. A mix of only disputed and paid products is not covered by the table and closes as dispute.
date_rules.next_weekday: the brief is silent; default 'following_week' used.
max_unclear: the brief is silent; default 3 used.
max_not_talk: the brief is silent; default 2 used.
purpose_is_decline: the brief is silent; default true (asking about the call instead of answering is treated as declining, told once why we ask).
Callback business_days_only false: the brief allows 'today or the next business day' without restricting today to business days.
promise_change: the brief is silent; the agent says the promise cannot be changed on this call.
sms_line empty: the brief requires no message after a recorded promise.
Products are handled in account order; the brief fixes no ordering.
